---
name: eskais-ui
description: Builds React screens with Eskais UI, a shadcn-style registry of agent-native components on Vercel UI SDK, in a project that installs them with shadcn add @eskais/... Use when choosing or composing Eskais components (Button, Form, Dialog, ConfirmDialog, Select, List, DataTable, AgentTaskBoard, Toast…), styling with its tokens, wiring agents to the UI, or when components.json lists the @eskais registry. Complements the official ui-sdk skill; load that one too.
---

# Eskais UI

Eskais UI components are UI SDK parts styled with Tailwind v4 and semantic tokens, copied into your project as source: the files under your `ui` alias (`src/components/ui/` by default) are yours to read and edit. Load the `ui-sdk` skill as well: everything it says about parts, controllers, change details and agents applies here unchanged.

Read a component's own file before you use it: the props, variants and the comment at the top are the API. This file says which component to reach for; the references say how the bigger ones work.

| Read                                 | When                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `references/forms.md`                | any form: fields, validation, server errors, dialogs, steps, floating labels            |
| `references/lists-and-navigation.md` | links, keyboard shortcuts, long lists and tables, a ⌘K search                           |
| `references/styling.md`              | spacing, tone, elevation, layers, motion, touch targets, narrow screens, type and icons |
| `references/toasts-and-testing.md`   | toasts, and testing toasts and alerts with Testing Library                              |
| `references/data-display.md`         | description lists, stat deltas, ring meters and value formats, table cells, chart data  |
| `references/agent-task-board.md`     | the AgentTaskBoard and its pieces                                                       |

Keeping screens fast (long lists, effects, React Compiler, motion) has its own skill, `eskais-perf`; building a throwaway mockup of a screen has `eskais-mockup`. Both install with `npx shadcn@latest add @eskais/eskais-perf-skill @eskais/eskais-mockup-skill`.

## Install

1. In `components.json`, add the registry once:
   `"registries": { "@eskais": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p-otero/eskais-ui/<ref>/public/r/{name}.json" }`, where `<ref>` is a tag like `v0.1.0`, or `main`.
2. Aliases: shadcn writes `registry:ui` files to `aliases.ui` and `registry:lib` files to `aliases.lib`, and rewrites the registry's `@/components/ui`, `@/lib` and `@/lib/utils` imports to `ui`, `lib` and `utils`, so any prefix works. Set `components`, `ui`, `utils` and `lib` (e.g. `"~/components"`, `"~/components/ui"`, `"~/lib/utils"`, `"~/lib"`), and make each resolve through `compilerOptions.paths` in the root `tsconfig.json`: shadcn ignores `tsconfig.app.json` and `references`, and writes into a literal `@/` folder when an alias doesn't resolve.
3. Put `@layer ui-sdk;` as the first line of the global stylesheet, above `@import "tailwindcss"`.
4. `npx shadcn@latest add @eskais/theme @eskais/font-geist @eskais/button` (any item; dependencies come along). `font-geist` bundles the default font from npm; without it the theme falls back to the system font. `font-inter` is the alternative.
5. Subpath imports work too: `"imports": { "#ui/*": "./src/components/ui/*", "#lib/*": "./src/lib/*", … }` in `package.json` with aliases `#ui`, `#lib`…, and `allowImportingTsExtensions`. Keep the extension out of the mapping: `ui` holds `.ts` and `.tsx` files, and shadcn writes the extension into each import (the Eskais README has the details). A `ui/` folder is optional: for a flat `src/components`, map `#ui/*` and `#components/*` to the same folder. shadcn then writes the imports between registry files as `#components/x.tsx` (the first alias that matches), not `#ui/x.tsx`; both resolve, so your own code can use either.
6. `theme` brings `utils`. Merge classes with its `cn` (`@/lib/utils`), never another one: it knows the theme's utilities, and a plain tailwind-merge drops `text-meta` from `cn("text-meta", "text-muted-foreground")`. Over a `lib/utils.ts` that `shadcn init` wrote, add with `--overwrite`.

## Choose

Each line is a need, then what to use. Props are listed by name; read the component file for their types.

- **An action, possibly async**: `Button`: return a Promise from `onClick` for pending, no double press; `loading` for work it didn't start (spinner in the leading icon's place, `aria-busy`, presses ignored, focus kept). `size="icon"` requires `aria-label`
- **An icon-only action**: `Button size="icon" aria-label` (also `Toggle` and `DialogTrigger`/`DialogClose`/`DrawerTrigger`/`PopoverTrigger`/`DropdownMenuTrigger`): shows the label, and `shortcut` keys, in a tooltip on hover and focus, never on touch; `tooltip={false}` when a visible label sits beside it, `tooltip="…"` or `{ content, side }` to describe it. `ControlTooltip label` for a control of your own. `eskais/icon-button-needs-label` flags one without them
- **A form with validation**: `Form schema defaultValues onSubmit messages label` + `FormField name label` around one control, `FormRootError`, `FormActions submitLabel`; see `references/forms.md`. `FieldSet legend` groups fields
- **A form in several steps**: `StepDialog trigger title schema defaultValues steps onSubmit labels` (or `StepForm` inline); see `references/forms.md`
- **A form in a modal**: `FormDialog trigger title schema defaultValues onSubmit submitLabel cancelLabel` with `FormField` children: closes on success, blocks Escape while pending, `confirmDiscard`, `reviewStep`
- **A labeled text input**: `Field` + `FieldLabel` + `Input`; `InputGroup` + `InputClear` for a clear button
- **A label inside the control**: `Field labelPlacement="in"` (floats up on focus or a value) or `"on"` (on the border); `Form labelPlacement` for every text field. See `references/forms.md`
- **A list of labels or tags**: `TokenInput tokenType="label" value onValueChange validate max tone` + `TokenInputEditor placeholder` in a `Field` or `FormField` (`string[]`, readonly arrays welcome): Enter or a comma adds, a paste splits on commas and line breaks, Backspace removes, Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes. Remove buttons are pointer-only, named by `labels.remove`. Without `tokenType`, UI SDK's text with mention or file tokens (`renderToken`, a `TriggerMenu` child)
- **Slides with their position**: `Carousel` parts; `CarouselStatus` shows "1 of 3" (`labels.status` translates it), announced politely only on change; `useCarouselState()` returns UI SDK's `page`, `pageCount` (null until measured), `playing` for your own header. Put the header inside `Carousel`, the region
- **A search box**: `SearchField label onSearch`: Enter runs `onSearch`, Escape clears only when there is text
- **A modal**: `Dialog` parts; `DialogContent size` (`sm`…`full`), `DialogBody` scrolls between header and footer, a bottom sheet on narrow screens unless `sheet={false}`; `dismissible={false}` + `onDismissAttempt` for unsaved changes; `initialFocus` on the content, never React `autoFocus`; keep it mounted and drive `open` (focus still returns if it unmounts while open)
- **"Are you sure?"**: `ConfirmDialog onConfirm`: a returned Promise shows pending, closes on success, shows the error on failure. Children render as a callout under the description, in the dialog's tone (`calloutTone` overrides). `labels={{ cancel }}` in the page's language ("Cancel" by default)
- **Static grouping and labels**: `Card` parts (a titled card is a `section` named by its title; `CardEyebrow`, `CardAction` as a direct child of `CardHeader`, which wraps it below the title once the title would drop under `--card-heading-basis` (11rem), `CardTitle headingLevel`, `surface`), `Badge tone`
- **Pick one of a list**: `Select options placeholder` (`{ value, label, disabled?, description? }`, or groups `{ label, options }`); `clearable="None"` adds a choice that sets `null`. `size="sm"` and `triggerProps` (`id`, `className`, `data-*`) style the trigger. Parts (`SelectTrigger`, `SelectContent`, `SelectItem`) still work as children
- **The platform's own picker**: `NativeSelect options placeholder clearable` in a `Field`: a styled native `<select>` for touch-heavy forms. Agents see it through its own primitive (a bare `<select>` or `FieldControl` is invisible to them)
- **Pick one of many, typed**: `Combobox` with `items` on the root, rendering options from `<ComboboxList>{(state) => state.items.map(…)}</ComboboxList>`. Static children aren't filtered, and agents then store the label instead of the value
- **Pick one of a few, all shown**: `RadioGroup` of `Radio` + `RadioIndicator`, each inside a `Label`; the `FieldLabel` names the group
- **An on/off setting**: `Switch` beside its `FieldLabel` in a `Field` (lays out as a row); it renders its own thumb
- **A number on a range**: `Slider` parts; a range names each `SliderThumb` with `aria-label`
- **A button that stays pressed**: `Toggle`; `ToggleGroup` (`multiple`, `deselectable={false}`) for several sharing one value
- **A one-time code**: `OTPInput` with `OTPInputSlot index` per character; one native input, so paste and autofill work
- **A typed, stepped number**: `NumberInput` + `NumberInputGroup`; step buttons are named "Decrease"/"Increase", override with `aria-label`
- **A label outside a Field**: `Label htmlFor`: names any control, including a radio group, slider or switch
- **Loading, error and empty for data**: `DataState status data error onRetry labels>{(data) => …}</DataState>` from `states`: never empty while pending or after an error, keeps the last success busy during a refetch; `data` counts only with `status="success"` (`placeholderData` for a busy first paint). Alone: `LoadingState label variant`, `ErrorState title message onRetry retryLabel details`, `Empty size` (`inline`, `panel`, `page`)
- **An icon**: `import { XIcon } from "lucide-react"` by name, as shadcn does; decorative by default. `Icon icon={XIcon} label` (from `icon`) when the icon alone carries meaning; see `references/styling.md`
- **A loading indicator**: `Spinner` (`size` sm, md, lg): decorative by default; `label` makes it a `role="status"`. Pulses instead of spinning under reduced motion
- **Progress or a reading**: `Progress` (`value={null}` is indeterminate) or `Meter`; the track renders its indicator. `Meter variant="ring"` with `MeterRing size` for a ring gauge; `format` on the root, or `formatValue` on the Value part for the visible text only; see `references/data-display.md`
- **A message in the page**: `Alert tone` with `AlertTitle`/`AlertDescription`, `action` for a trailing button; `live` for messages that appear later (`role="alert"` for warning/destructive, `role="status"` otherwise)
- **A status label**: `StatusPill tone` (the shared tones plus `muted`), with an optional `dot`/`pulse`; `StatusDot tone label` alone
- **Related items as chips**: `DependencyChips` with an `aria-label`; pass `onSelect` to make each chip a button agents can press
- **A number that may be guessed**: `QuantityValue` with `{ value, quality, source }`: unknown shows `—`, never 0; estimated shows `~`
- **A time**: `RelativeTime` with one `useNow()` per screen passed down as `now`, not one timer per time
- **Pass/fail criteria**: `AcceptanceList`, and `AcceptanceBar` with `countAcceptance` for a compact summary
- **Summary figures**: `StatGroup` of `Stat` parts; `StatDelta value comparison invert` for a change, read in words; see `references/data-display.md`
- **An entity's properties**: `DescriptionList layout columns labels` (`stacked`, `inline`, `grid`) of `DescriptionItem` > `DescriptionTerm` + `DescriptionDetails mono copyable`; an empty value reads `labels.empty`; see `references/data-display.md`
- **Columns of items**: `Board` with `BoardColumn` (collapsible, groups, `empty`); no drag and drop
- **Which agent ran**: `AgentBadge agent requested?`: a provider avatar (initials on a stable color, or your `avatars`), long model ids truncate in the middle, a marker when what ran differs
- **Is an agent alive**: `LivenessIndicator` with `liveness` from your data; it never infers it from times
- **Task or attempt status**: `TaskStatusPill`, `AttemptStatusPill`, `ContextModePill`
- **Tokens and cost**: `UsageGrid` (dense tiles, for a detail view), `UsageTable` (rows, side-by-side columns) or `UsageStat`; unknown stays `—`
- **An agent task's attempts**: `AttemptTimeline`; older attempts collapse past five
- **Approve or reject a proposal**: `ProposalActions` with `agentApproval` (`"confirm"` by default, `"allow"`, `"deny"`)
- **A whole board of agent tasks**: `AgentTaskBoard` with `tasks` and `mode`; see `references/agent-task-board.md`
- **One agent task, compact**: `TaskCard` (selects through a stretched button; chips and proposal buttons stay their own tab stops)
- **One agent task, in full**: `TaskDetailDialog` (modal, or `presentation="drawer"`) or `TaskDetailPanel` (non-modal); Escape and a close button call `onClose`
- **A bar pinned to an edge**: `Floating side align strategy` (`sticky` default, `fixed`, `absolute`) + `FloatingContent`; put a `FilterBar` or other UI SDK controls inside. Sticky bars go last in their scroll container
- **Files and screenshots on an item**: `AttachmentStrip attachments aria-label max size onOpen`: image thumbnails open a built-in `Lightbox`, files open `href`; `+N` reveals the rest. `AttachmentThumb` alone. Agents get `openAttachment(id)`
- **One image of a set, full size**: `Lightbox items index onIndexChange open onOpenChange`: arrow keys, counter, fit or actual size, open original; `srcDark` follows the theme without a flash. Agents get `next`, `previous`, `goTo(index)`
- **Where work is in a pipeline**: `StageTrack stages current aria-label` (`variant="pill"` for only the current stage, `getHref` for links); `StageFilter stages counts value onValueChange` is a toggle group to filter by stage
- **Dense rows or entity cards**: `List aria-label` + `ListGroup label count` + `ListItem id title leading subtitle status meta trailing actions href/onSelect selected`; `variant="card"` for cards; `value`/`onValueChange` on `List` makes it a Listbox. Agents get `select(id)`
- **Keyboard shortcuts**: `useShortcut(keys, handler, { scope, enabled, description })` from `shortcuts` (`"u"`, `"mod+k"`, `"g i"`); `ShortcutScope name label active` for a region or an open panel; `Button shortcut="u"`, `DropdownMenuItem shortcut`; `ShortcutsDialog` once for `?`, with a `ShortcutsDialogTrigger` inside for touch. See `references/lists-and-navigation.md`
- **Tabs that switch on press**: `Tabs activateOnPress` / `SegmentedControl activateOnPress` (off by default): a mouse or pen press selects before release, like Linear and macOS; touch stays on release so scrolling doesn't select; keyboard and agents unchanged. Only for reversible view switches: actions, menu items and anything that submits always act on release
- **An inspector beside a list**: `SidePanel open onOpenChange title description actions returnFocus narrow`: non-modal, Escape closes it and returns focus to the row; `Button shortcut` inside runs while it's open; `narrow` picks `stack`, `overlay` or `sheet` on phones (`references/styling.md`). The `inbox` block composes List, SidePanel and shortcuts
- **Thousands of rows**: `List items getItemId renderItem itemText`, flat `<ListItem id>` children, or `DataTable`: past 200 rows only the rows in view render (`virtualize="auto"`, `estimateSize`), every row stays reachable by keyboard, agents and find in page
- **A page's column**: `PageLayout width header` (`dense`, `wide`, `full`; `variant="workspace"` for app screens). Renders `<main id="main">` only with `as="main"`, since the shell may own `<main>`; never a live region
- **A titled block on a page**: `Section title eyebrow description action footer headingLevel surface padding`: Card composed; `surface="dashed"` for a create tile, `"none"` for no box
- **The top of a landing page**: `Hero eyebrow title titleMuted titleBreak description actions aside install align decoration headingLevel` (block): side by side or centered by container width, the install command a copyable CodeBlock
- **A page section's heading**: `SectionHeading eyebrow title description actions align headingLevel headingId` (block); give the `<section aria-labelledby>` the `headingId`
- **A grid of feature tiles**: `Bento columns` + `BentoTile span rowSpan eyebrow title description href onFollow` (block): one column, two from 48rem of container, `columns` from 64rem; children are the live demo
- **Numbered instructions**: `Steps orientation` + `Step title description` (block): an `<ol>`, side by side on wide containers; children such as a CodeBlock
- **A page footer**: `SiteFooter brand description groups bottom` (block): groups are `{ title, links }`, each a named navigation of muted `Link`s that take any Link prop
- **A documentation page**: `DocsLayout topbar sidebar header toc as` (block): an app shell, a `Topbar` with `<SidebarTrigger {...sidebar.triggerProps} />` in `leading`, a `Sidebar {...sidebar.sidebarProps} collapse="hide" trigger={false}` that sticks under it (`--topbar-height`) at the full height, `header` (a `DocsBreadcrumb`) above the page, with `const sidebar = useSidebarState({ storageKey })`. Without a topbar, `--docs-top` in `style` clears a header of your own. `DocsToc items` with `useTocItems(ref)`, `DocsPager previous next`
- **A new landing page**: Copy `@eskais/landing-page`: Hero, SectionHeading, Bento, Steps and SiteFooter with the copy in one `content` object. Edit props and slots, don't hand-write layout
- **A public site's header**: `SiteHeader label brand items actions renderLink`: a floating pill; links that don't fit move into "More" (measured, in order), `items` with children become dropdowns, a drawer with every link on narrow screens, `data-scrolled` once the page scrolls. Put a `SkipLink` before it
- **An app screen's header**: `Topbar brand leading center centerCompact trailing`: sticky, a bottom border, `centerCompact` replaces the centre on narrow screens. `<Topbar leading={<SidebarTrigger controller={sidebar} collapsed={collapsed} />}>` is the one pattern for every width: with the `Sidebar` given the same `createSidebarController()` and `trigger={false}`, it collapses the rail on wide screens and opens the sidebar's drawer on narrow ones, where the `Sidebar` then renders no drawer button of its own (`narrowTrigger` overrides that)
- **Navigation on a phone**: `MobileNav label items overflow`: a bottom tab bar of five slots (icon over label, `current`, `badge`). Up to five `items` fill them when there is no `overflow`; with `overflow` or more than five items, four stay and the fifth slot is More, which opens the rest. Labels shrink to the meta size and wrap to two lines rather than truncate, shown at `narrow:` only unless `always`. Hide the `Sidebar` with `narrow:hidden` and give the page `narrow:mb-(--mobile-nav-offset)` so it ends above the bar
- **Skip past navigation**: `SkipLink` first in `<body>` (text required; `target` is an id or ref, default `"main"`; focuses it without changing the URL, safe in hash routers), with `PageLayout as="main"` or your own `<main id="main">`
- **Many tabs in little space**: `TabsList` scrolls on its own when its tabs don't fit (`scrollable="auto"`): edge fades, pointer-only scroll buttons (aria-hidden, not for agents), arrow keys reach every tab, works in rtl. `scrollable={false}` opts out
- **A page title**: `PageHeader title eyebrow description actions tabs breadcrumb headingLevel`; `tabs` holds a `TabsList` inside a `Tabs` that wraps the page; actions wrap below the title on narrow screens
- **A date and a time together**: `DateTimePicker value onValueChange min max locale timeZone labels={{ time }}` in a `Field`: one local `"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm"` value; the time has its own label, which must not repeat the date label's words; `TimeInput` alone for a time of day
- **Dates, layout or data table**: `Calendar`/`DatePicker` (ISO, `locale`, `timeZone`), `Carousel`, `Resizable`, `Sidebar` (rail, drawer), `DataTable` (typed columns with `wrap`, `cellClassName`, `headerClassName`; `renderPagination`), `PageHeader`, `FilterBar` (a Toolbar)
- **Code to show or copy**: `CodeBlock code language title` (`ts`, `tsx`, `js`, `jsx`, `json`, `css`, `html`, `bash`, `md`, `diff`; parsers load on first use), `lineNumbers`, `highlightLines`, `wrap`, `maxHeight`, `onCopy`; `CodeTabs files aria-label` for several files; `Code` inline. Colours are `--syntax-*` tokens; agents read the code and call `copy`
- **A link**: `Link variant` (`inline` in prose, `nav`/`muted` in lists, `standalone`, `plain` inside a styled row or card), `external`, `newTab`, `current`, `render` (a router link). `onFollow` takes plain clicks for client routing and gives agents a `follow` action; links without it are invisible to agents. `ButtonLink variant size` (from `button`) for a call to action. Both follow on press (`references/lists-and-navigation.md`)
- **Menus, site navigation, paging, ⌘K**: `ContextMenu`, `Menubar`, `NavigationMenu`, `Breadcrumb`, `Pagination page pageCount onPageChange labels`, `CommandDialog` + `Command` (pass `shortcut="mod+k"` to the trigger to opt in); `Accordion`, `HoverCard` for disclosure and link previews
- **A chart**: `ChartContainer config aria-labelledby` + Recharts (`accessibilityLayer`), `ChartTooltip`/`ChartLegend` + `…Content`, `ChartDataTable data labelKey keys` (typed from your rows). Every series meets 3:1 on the card, aqua (`--chart-3`) only just, so still add a legend or value labels. Series with a meaning take `var(--series-positive)`, `--series-negative`, `--series-target` or `--series-remaining`
- **Write or show Markdown**: `MarkdownEditor label value onChange` (debounced; `onConflict` when a new `value` meets unsent edits) keeps the Markdown byte for byte and shows marks only while the caret is in their span; `codeLanguages={markdownCodeLanguages}` from `@eskais/markdown-editor-languages` is opt-in, `labels={markdownEditorLabelsEs}` for Spanish. `MarkdownView markdown` renders it read-only

## Separate the layers

- **Generic UI** (open/close, pending, focus, dismissal): UI SDK, already inside the components. Don't rebuild it with `useState` + `useEffect`.
- **Reusable app behavior** (confirm before deleting, search on Enter): an Eskais UI composed component such as `ConfirmDialog` or `SearchField`.
- **Business logic** (requests, toasts, cache invalidation): always in your callback (`onConfirm`, `onSearch`). Components never run side effects of their own.

## Agents

- Create one bridge in the app with `createAgent` from `@ui-sdk/react/agent`. Pass an `allow` that checks `step.confirm` and asks a person.
- `ConfirmDialog` with `tone="destructive"` requires `agentConfirm`: a sentence saying what confirming does. It becomes `data-agent-confirm`, so agents must get approval.
- `SearchField` exposes a `submit` action to agents only when `onSearch` is set.
- Show the approval prompt as its own alert dialog (`createConfirm` from `@ui-sdk/react/alert-dialog`), not as page content: when the agent opens a modal such as `ConfirmDialog`, the rest of the page goes inert and an inline prompt can't be clicked.
- Every control needs a name a person would recognize; the agent finds it by that name.
- Test every interface with the agent test from the ui-sdk skill (`.agents/skills/ui-sdk/references/agent-ready.md`).

## Style

- Use the variants (`variant`, `size`) and the semantic tokens: `background`, `foreground`, `primary`, `secondary`, `muted`, `accent`, `destructive`, `success`, `warning`, `info`, `border`, `input`, `input-strong`, `field`, `ring`, `overlay`, and `link`/`link-soft` for link text and a caret (4.5:1 on background, card and muted). `accent` is a surface (hover and selected fills) only: never a text colour or a stroke. For a stroke use `border-input-strong`, `border-primary` or `ring-ring`; for coloured text, `text-link`.
- Text fields take a soft `border-input` edge on a `bg-field` fill; checkboxes, radios and switch tracks, which nothing else identifies, take `input-strong` (3:1).
- Style state with UI SDK attributes: `data-pending`, `data-disabled`, `data-open`, `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style`.
- Use the shape and density tokens instead of fixed sizes: `rounded-control`, `rounded-choice` (checkbox, textarea), `rounded-surface`, `h-control` (`-sm`, `-lg`), `shadow-surface`, and the spacing roles below. Surfaces that may turn glassy use `bg-<color>/(--glass-opacity)` and `backdrop-surface`.
- Theme and color scheme are app-level: `createAppearance({ colorScheme: "system" })` and `<Appearance appearance={…}>` from `@eskais/appearance` keep `.dark`, `data-color-scheme` and `data-theme` on `<html>` in sync; call `appearance.apply()` before the first render. Without any script the theme still follows `prefers-color-scheme: dark`, unless `<html>` has `data-color-scheme="light"` or `class="light"` (render one from the server for a saved light choice). The `dark:` variant does too: the theme item appends its `@custom-variant dark { … }` block below the one-line `@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *))` that shadcn writes, and Tailwind uses the last one, so keep it last. Don't add a theme prop to a component.
- Tones: `neutral`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive` say what a status means; `violet` is a category tone (a label or kind), never a status. For a tinted chip or surface use the soft tokens, `bg-{tone}-soft text-{tone}-soft-foreground border-{tone}-border`, not `bg-{tone}/10`; for a loading placeholder, `Skeleton` or `bg-skeleton`.
- Colour: set the seeds `--brand`, `--link-brand` (links and the caret, a blue by default), `--neutral-hue`, `--neutral-chroma` (and `--radius`) in `:root`; primary, its foreground, ring, accent and greys derive from them in light and dark. Or use a preset from `@eskais/palettes` with `data-palette="blue"` (`neutral`, `violet`, `green`, `orange`) on any element, or `createAppearance({ palette })`. To take over one colour, set that token in `:root` or `.dark`. Keep a custom brand at 4.5:1 on the background.
- Themes are attribute scopes, not separate components: `data-theme="compact"` or `data-theme="glass"` on any element, nested freely. A theme only sets tokens; never branch on the theme in a component.
- Pass layout classes (margin, width, grid placement) through `className`. To change how a component looks, edit its file in `components/ui/`, which you own.
- Optional: `npx shadcn add @eskais/lint-rules` adds an oxlint config with the `react` and `ui-tailwind` presets of `@p-otero/oxlint-rules` (hooks, React Compiler checks, `p-otero/spacing-tokens`) and the `@shadcn/lint` rules (`no-restyle`, `no-raw-colors`…). Extend it from `.oxlintrc.json`.

## Keep it small

- Keep components short; split a file before it passes about 200 lines.
- Every screen state needs a decision: loading, empty, error, disabled, confirming.
- No `App*` wrapper layer and no providers the consumer must mount.

# AgentTaskBoard

Part of the `eskais-ui` skill.

## AgentTaskBoard

`npx shadcn add @eskais/agent-task-board` installs the board and every piece it uses.

- **Snapshot or live.** `mode="snapshot"` needs `generatedAt`: it is the board's "now", shown in a banner, and times never refresh. It shows no approve or reject actions. `mode="live"` refreshes times every 30 s, paused while the page is hidden; pass `now` only for tests and screenshots.
- **One clock.** The board calls `useNow` once and passes `now` down. When you compose `TaskCard` or `TaskDetailPanel` yourself, do the same: one `useNow()` per screen, never one timer per time.
- **Labels.** English by default. Override any string with `labels={{ columns: { done: "Shipped" } }}`, or pass `labels={agentTaskBoardLabelsEs}` from `@/components/ui/agent-task-board` for Spanish, including the pieces inside (status, liveness, usage, attempts). Pass `locale` and `timeZone` for formatting.
- **Agents.** The board's root exposes `selectTask`, `setView` (`"board"`, `"table"`, `"backlog"`), `filter` (`project`, `profile`, `model`, `query`, and `stage` as a list of stage ids, where `NO_STAGE` or the "No stage" label picks tasks without a location), `openThread` and `openLink` (`openLink(taskId, labelOrHref)`, with `onOpenLink`). A Button rendered as a link has no `press` for agents, so links open through that action. In live mode with `onApproveProposal`/`onRejectProposal`, `agentApproval` decides what an agent may do: `"confirm"` (default) asks a person through your bridge's `allow`, `"allow"` acts without asking, `"deny"` hides the actions from agents. People's buttons are the same either way.
- **Detail.** `detailPresentation="dialog"` (default) opens a selected task in an `xl` dialog, two columns from 56rem; `"drawer"` slides it in from the right; `"side"` keeps a non-modal panel so the board stays usable while reading. With a modal open, the board's controls are hidden from agents, but its `selectTask`, `filter` and `setView` still work.
- **Columns.** The collapse toggle ends each header (shown on hover, focus, touch or while collapsed). `columnAccent="tint"` (default) marks each column with its tone, `taskStatusAccentTones` overridden by `columnTones`; the status icons follow. Order comes from `columns`.
- **Links.** `TaskView.links` (`pull-request`, `branch`, `commit`, `issue`, `external`, with an optional `state`) list in the detail's side column; a card shows an icon link to its pull request. `renderLink` replaces each, `onOpenLink` takes over the click. A thread with `href` or `onOpenThread` gets an "Open thread" button with its id in the tooltip.
- **Attachments.** `TaskView.attachments` (the `Attachment` type of `@eskais/attachments`) show as an `AttachmentStrip` in the detail's main column, images opening a `Lightbox`; a card shows a paperclip count. Agents use the strip's `openAttachment(id)`. `renderAttachments(task)` replaces the strip.
- **Location.** Pass `stages` (the `Stage[]` of `@eskais/stage-track`, in order) and set `TaskView.location = { stage, href? }`: cards show a `StagePill`, the detail's side column a `StageTrack`, and the toolbar a `StageFilter` row with counts that sets `filters.stage`. Its last toggle, "No stage" (`labels.filters.noStage`), sets `NO_STAGE` (exported from the board) for tasks without a location; it shows when some task has none, and `stageFilterNone` forces it on or off. `renderLocation(task)` replaces the track.
- **Backlog.** `view="backlog"` lists proposals and to-do tasks that aren't ready as `ListItem` rows in two `ListGroup`s with counts; live proposals keep Approve/Reject. A row opens the detail like a card. `renderBacklogActions(task)` adds your controls (a copy-command button) after Approve/Reject in each row, snapshot mode included; `renderCardActions(task)` does the same at the end of a card (pass a stable function: cards are memoized). Use the registry's `Button` and name it after the task ("Copy command for T-011"). The row's own button reads that text too, so an agent acts on the ref from its snapshot.
- **Filter controls.** `filterControls` lists the built-in controls that show (`"query"`, `"project"`, `"profile"`, `"model"`, `"stage"`; all by default). Leave one out when the host renders its own, such as a project picker: pass that value in `filters`, where it still applies, and agents can still set every key with `filter`. "Clear filters" clears only the visible controls.
- **Density.** `density="auto"` (default) applies compact shape and spacing while the board is 75rem wide or less; `"compact"` always, `"comfortable"` never. It needs `@eskais/theme-compact`.
- **State.** `view`, `filters`, `columns` and `selectedTaskId` are each controlled or uncontrolled (`defaultView`, `defaultFilters`, `defaultSelectedTaskId`). Cancelled tasks are hidden until `columns` shows them.
- **Static.** It works in a single HTML file with no network (a snapshot to attach to a report): every asset is local.

# Forms

Part of the `eskais-ui` skill.

## Forms

`npx shadcn add @eskais/form` brings react-hook-form and `@hookform/resolvers`. The schema is any Standard Schema: Zod, Valibot, ArkType or Effect Schema.

- **Fields.** `<FormField name label description required>` wraps one control and binds it by `name`: `Input`, `Textarea`, `NumberInput`, `Select`, `Combobox`, `Checkbox`, `Switch`, `RadioGroup`, `Slider`, `DatePicker`, `SegmentedControl`, `ToggleGroup`, `TokenInput` (a `string[]` with `tokenType`). Checkbox and Switch bind `checked`, the rest `value`/`onValueChange`. A control's own module can add an adapter to `formControlAdapters` (exported from `field` and `form`). For your own control pass `bind="checked"`, an adapter, or `render={(field) => …}`; inside it, `useFormField()` returns `value`, `onChange`, `invalid`, `error`. Give every field a default value.
- **Required.** A field the schema rejects when empty gets an `aria-hidden` asterisk (`text-destructive`) and its control `required`. Detection probes the schema synchronously with the default values, so it needs a schema that reports every issue (Zod, Valibot, ArkType); otherwise pass `required`. `required={false}` drops the marker. `requiredLabel="required"` (on `Form` or `FormField`, in the page's language) adds words for screen readers; they join the field's name, so agents and `getByRole` see "Email required". Unset, screen readers announce the control's own required state.
- **Typed names.** `const { Form, FormField, useFormInstance, useFormWatch, useFormFieldArray } = createForm<typeof schema>()` at module level: the same components, with `name` checked against the schema's input (`tags.${number}.label` included).

  ```tsx
  const schema = z.object({ name: z.string().min(1), email: z.email() })
  const Profile = createForm<typeof schema>()

  <Profile.Form schema={schema} defaultValues={{ name: "", email: "" }} onSubmit={save} label="Profile">
    <Profile.FormField name="email" label="Email"><Input type="email" /></Profile.FormField>
  </Profile.Form>
  ```

- **Submit.** `onSubmit(values, { setError })` gets the parsed values. A returned Promise shows the submit Button's `loading`, disables the fields (`disableWhilePending={false}` keeps them) and ignores a second submit. Don't add your own pending state.
- **Server errors.** Throw `new FormServerError(message, { email: "Taken" })`, an object `{ fieldErrors, message }`, or a Standard Schema issue list (`toFormErrors` reads all three). Field errors land on their fields; the message, and errors for fields that aren't rendered, in `<FormRootError />` (an `Alert tone="destructive" live`). Any other error shows its `message` there. Focus then moves to the first invalid field, or to the root error.
- **Messages.** English by default. `messages={formMessagesEs}`, your own dictionary (strings with `{min}`, `{max}`, `{label}`, or functions), or a function of the issue for any i18n library: `messages={(issue) => t(`form.${issue.code}`, { ...issue.params, field: issue.label })}`, or `createFormMessages(t)`. Return `undefined` to fall back to the defaults, then to the schema's own message. `<FormField messages>` wins over the form's.
- **Issues.** `{ code, field, label?, params, message? }`. Codes: `required` (an empty value), `minLength`/`maxLength` and `minItems`/`maxItems` (`params.min`/`max`), `min`/`max`, `email`, `url`, `pattern`, `invalid` (no known validator; `message` is the schema's), `server` (a plain-text server error). A schema message that looks like a key (`"form.email.taken"`) is its own code, so schemas can carry translation keys. A server error may be `{ code, params?, message? }` instead of text: `{ fieldErrors: { email: { code: "email.taken" } } }`.
- **Schemas without codes.** Effect Schema (and any Standard Schema whose issues carry only `message` and `path`) reaches `messages` as `invalid`, or `required` for an empty value. Put the code in the message: `formIssueMessage(code, params)` writes `@@form:code` or `@@form:code|{json}` (a reserved prefix, so it never reads prose as a code), and the form reads it back as `issue.code` and `issue.params`, with `issue.message` `undefined`. Every code round-trips, built-in or dotted. The earlier `code|{json}` and bare dotted keys still read. Use a dotted key for your i18n library or a built-in code for the built-in dictionaries: `Schema.String.pipe(Schema.minLength(3, { message: () => formIssueMessage("minLength", { min: 3 }) }))`. Without a translation, the key shows without its params. There is no Effect adapter: its issues hold nothing more to read.
- **Actions.** `<FormActions submitLabel pendingLabel cancel onCancel secondaryAction>` stacks on narrow screens. For a busy state outside the form, `disabled` disables submit and cancel, `submitDisabled` only submit, and `pending` forces the pending look; with any of them the form doesn't submit, from Enter, code or an agent. `tone="destructive"` requires `confirm`, the sentence an agent must show a person; it becomes `data-agent-confirm` on the submit button.
- **In a dialog.** `FormDialog` takes the Form props plus `trigger` (or `open`/`onOpenChange`), `title`, `description`, `size`, `submitLabel`, `cancelLabel`, `pendingLabel`, `secondaryAction` and `returnFocus`. `onOpenChange(open, details)` and `onOpenChangeComplete(open, details)` (after the transition) say why in `details.reason`: `submit`, `cancel`, `escape`, `outside`, `dismiss`, or `trigger` when it opens. The body scrolls between the header and the actions; on narrow screens it is a bottom sheet. It closes when `onSubmit` resolves, and a thrown error keeps it open. Escape, outside presses and Cancel do nothing while pending. `confirmDiscard="Discard changes?"` (with `discardLabel`, `keepEditingLabel`) asks before closing with unsaved changes. `reviewStep={{ render: (values) => …, editLabel, confirmLabel }}` validates, shows a review, and runs `onSubmit` on confirm; a server field error returns to the fields. `prepare: async (values, { form }) => ({ values } | { error })` runs first with the submit pending. Returned `values` are reviewed and submitted and also written into the form (`setValue` per top-level key), so Edit shows them; they must pass the schema as input too. Or write through `form.setValue` and return nothing: the form's values are parsed again and reviewed. Returned `values` win over what `prepare` wrote. `editable: (state) => !state.error` hides Edit, and `title: (step) => step === "review" ? "Check the order" : "New order"` follows the step.
- **Instance.** Inside a `Form`, `useFormInstance<Values>()` is the typed react-hook-form instance (`trigger`, `setValue`, `getValues`, `control`, `formState`). Its `watch` re-renders the Form, not your component: use `useFormWatch(name)`. `useFormFieldArray(name, options)` wraps `useFieldArray`; key rows by `field.id` (or, when the items carry their own `id`, by the property `keyName: "fieldKey"` names) and name fields `` `tags.${index}.label` ``. `form-context.ts` is internal: import only from `@/components/ui/form`.
- **Steps.** `StepDialog` (or `StepForm` inline) splits one schema into `steps: { id, title, description?, render: (form) => …, fields?, validate? }[]`. Next and Enter validate only that step's fields (`fields`, or its mounted `FormField`s) and then `validate(values)`, which returns nothing or an error in any shape `onSubmit` throws. Back keeps values. The last step submits through `onSubmit`; a failed validation or a server field error returns to the step that holds the field. Focus moves to the step heading on Next and Back. The progress list marks the current step with `aria-current="step"`. `onStepChange(id, { index, previous, direction })`, `step`/`defaultStep`, and `labels` (`next`, `back`, `submit`, `progress`, `cancel`) in the page's language. Agents press Next, Back and the submit button by name. `StepDialog` `onOpenChange(open, details)` gives `details.reason` (`submit`, `done`, `cancel`, `escape`, `outside`, `dismiss`, `trigger`). To show the outcome in the dialog instead of closing it, pass `resultStep={{ title, render: (result, { close, restart }) => … }}`: `result` is what `onSubmit` resolved with, focus moves to the result heading, Done (`labels.done`) and Escape close it (reason `done` or `escape`), and `restart()` starts over from step 1 with the default values.
- **Label placement.** `labelPlacement` on `Form` sets a default for its fields, plain `Field`s in the floating layout included; `labelPlacement` on a `FormField` or `Field` overrides it (`top` keeps the label above); see "Floating labels".
- **Agents.** Fields are their own UI SDK parts, so agents fill them by label. With a `label` (or `aria-labelledby`), the form itself offers `submit` and `reset`; a destructive form hides them so the gated button is the only way.

## Floating labels

`<Field labelPlacement="top" | "in" | "on">` (and `Form`/`FormField labelPlacement`) moves the `FieldLabel`. It stays a real `<label>`, so people, screen readers and agents name the control the same way in every placement.

- **`top`** (default): above the control.
- **`in`**: inside the control like a placeholder; it floats up and shrinks on focus, once the control has a value, or while its popup is open. The control grows by `--field-label-offset` to fit both, so nothing moves when it floats. A placeholder would sit under the resting label, so it shows only while the control is focused: write it as a format hint, never as the only instructions.
- **`on`**: on the control's top border, cutting the line. It is drawn over `--field-label-surface`, which cards (`field-label-surface-card`), dialogs and drawers (`field-label-surface-popover`) and floating surfaces set to their fill; the page background otherwise. Set it yourself on another coloured surface. Placeholders show as usual.
- **Controls.** Input, InputGroup (the label starts after a leading icon), Textarea, Select, NativeSelect, NumberInput, DatePicker, DateTimePicker, Combobox and TokenInput (it grows with its chips; `on` leaves room under the label). A Form's default reaches only those, in a `FormField` or in a plain `Field` inside the Form (a read-only Textarea, say) that doesn't set its own and is in the floating layout: a `FieldLabel`, then the control, then only a `FieldDescription` or `FieldError`, with no padding in its `className` (the label is placed from the Field's box, so padding or other content would put it over the value). Any other Field, and a padded `FormField`, keeps its label on top unless it sets `labelPlacement` itself; Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroup, Slider, SegmentedControl and ToggleGroup keep their label on top. A control of your own floats on `:placeholder-shown`, `data-filled` or `data-open`: give its input `useFloatingPlaceholder(placeholder)` and add it to `floatingLabelControls` so a Form's default applies.
- **State.** The description and error stay below. An invalid field turns the label `destructive`; a focused one `foreground`. The motion is a transform, collapsed under reduced motion. The states come from the theme's `field-floated` variant, so update `@eskais/theme` with the components.

# Styling

Part of the `eskais-ui` skill.

## Spacing

Pick spacing by the relationship between the things it separates, never by a number; each role tightens under `data-theme="compact"`.

| Utility                           | Role                                                                             |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `gap-inline`                      | icon + text, or parts inside one control, chip or row                            |
| `gap-items`                       | siblings in a list or stack: cards in a column, chips, buttons, form fields      |
| `gap-group`                       | groups inside a surface: header vs body, dialog sections                         |
| `gap-section`                     | surfaces on a page                                                               |
| `px-inset-chip` / `py-inset-chip` | pills, badges, chips, kbd                                                        |
| `px-inset-item` / `py-inset-item` | menu and list items, small cards, table cells                                    |
| `px-control-x`                    | buttons, inputs, selects                                                         |
| `p-inset-surface`                 | cards, dialogs, panels, popovers (`p-surface` is an alias)                       |
| `p-control-inset`                 | the rim of a control-height bar around `-sm` items (tab list, segmented control) |

- `inline`, `items`, `group`, `section` and `inset-surface` work with any spacing utility (`p-inline`, `pb-group`, `-mx-inline`). The chip and item insets are `px-`/`py-` only; otherwise use the variable, as in `-mx-(--item-padding-x)`.
- Components never set their own outer margin; the parent spaces children with `gap-*`. Pass margin through `className` only when composing.
- Sizes (`size-*`, `h-*`, `w-*`) aren't spacing; prefer `h-control` and friends.
- With `@eskais/lint-rules`, `p-otero/spacing-tokens` warns on numeric spacing (`gap-2`, `md:px-1`). The exceptions are `0`, `px`, and a disable comment that gives the reason.

## Tone

Status meaning has one vocabulary across Badge, Alert, StatusPill, StatusDot, Progress, Meter and Toast: `tone` is `neutral`, `info`, `success`, `warning` or `destructive` (`Tone` from `@/lib/tone`). Badge's `variant` is only its untoned look (`default`, `secondary`, `outline`); `variant="success"` and friends still work but are deprecated. A toast's tone comes from its type (`toastTone`: `error` is `destructive`).

## Elevation

Surfaces (cards, columns, panels) use `shadow-surface`. Anything that floats (popover, menu, list popup, toast, dialog, a `Floating` bar) uses the floating level: `surface-floating`, or its parts `shadow-floating`, `rounded-floating`, `bg-floating`, `backdrop-floating`, `border-floating-border`. Tokens: `--floating-shadow`, `--floating-radius`, `--floating-backdrop`, `--floating-opacity`, `--floating-border`, `--floating-offset`. The fill is translucent and blurred by default, opaque without `backdrop-filter` or with reduced transparency. `data-elevation="flat"` on any ancestor removes the depth. Never use viewport-height units (`vh`, `dvh`, `h-screen`) to place floating UI; it takes its position from its container.

## Layers and motion

Stack with `z-sticky` < `z-overlay` (dialogs) < `z-popover` < `z-toast`, never a number. Time transitions with `duration-micro` (140ms: hover, popovers, tooltips), `duration-panel` (180ms: accordion, sidebar, toasts) or `duration-dialog` (200ms), with `ease-standard`. Reduced motion is handled globally by the theme.

## Touch targets

On touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) buttons, toggles, tabs, segmented items, checkboxes, radios and switches get an invisible hit area of at least 44px (`--control-height-touch`); sidebar items and label rows around a choice grow to 44px. Desktop looks the same. Give a new small control the `touch-target` class; where controls stack tighter than 44px, grow the row with `pointer-coarse:min-h-(--control-height-touch)` instead.

## Narrow screens

`narrow:` applies at 760px viewport width and below (`flex-row narrow:flex-col`). It is unrelated to the `compact` density theme, which changes sizes at any width. Prefer container queries for components placed in panels of different widths.

`SidePanel narrow` decides where an inspector goes at that width: `"stack"` (default) keeps it in the page flow, full width, and wraps its flex parent so it lands below the list, hiding nothing and trapping no focus; `"overlay"` covers its positioned parent, for a panel that should show instead of the list (a tall scroller in a bounded column); `"sheet"` opens it as a modal bottom `Drawer` that takes focus and returns it to `returnFocus()` on close.

## Typography

Pick text size by role, not by number: `text-meta` (eyebrows; with `tracking-meta`, uppercase if you want), `text-caption`, `text-body-sm`, `text-body`, `text-title-sm` (card titles), `text-title` (dialog titles), `text-display-sm` (page titles, stat values), `text-display`, and `text-entry` for text a person types (16px on touch screens, so iOS doesn't zoom into a focused field; never set `maximum-scale` or `user-scalable=no` instead). Each sets size, line height and weight, and tightens under `data-theme="compact"`: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 18, 24 and 28px by default. `tracking-tight` (-0.012em) suits titles; `font-mono` is Geist Mono (installed by `font-geist`).

## Icons

Components import their icons from `lucide-react` by name (`ChevronDownIcon`, `XIcon`, `CheckIcon`, `SearchIcon`…), and every item that does lists it in `dependencies`, so shadcn installs it. Browse the set on lucide.dev; the site's Icons guide shows the ones the registry uses.

- **Decorative**: lucide sets `aria-hidden` unless the icon gets an `aria-*`, `role` or `title` prop, so an icon beside text needs nothing. An icon-only button is named by the button, and shows that name in a tooltip: `<Button size="icon" aria-label="Delete"><TrashIcon /></Button>`.
- **Meaningful**: when nothing else says it, `<Icon icon={TriangleExclamationPointIcon} label="Blocked" />` renders `role="img"` with that name. `Icon` takes any SVG component.
- **Size**: controls set it (`[&_svg]:size-4` in Button, Toggle, menu items, inputs; `size-3` in Badge), and those classes beat lucide's `size` prop. Elsewhere: `size-3.5` beside `text-body-sm`, `size-4` beside `text-body`, `size-5` beside a title. Unsized, an icon is 24px.
- **Colour**: `currentColor`; use a tone's text colour (`text-success`), and still say the status in words. Alert colours its first-child icon by tone; Toast draws its tone's icon itself.
- **Swap the set**: only the import lines change. Don't hand-draw an icon as inline `<svg>`; drawings that aren't icons (a spinner's arc, status rings) are the exception.

# Toasts and testing

Part of the `eskais-ui` skill.

## Toasts

- Place `<ToastStack />` once (or pass a `toaster` from `createToaster()`), and call `toast()`, `toast.success()`… from your handlers.
- Its close buttons are named "Dismiss". Pass `labels={{ close: "Cerrar" }}` in the page's language (`closeLabel` is deprecated).
- Each type leads with a decorative icon in its tone colour: `info` a circled i, `success` a check, `warning` a triangle, `error` a circled exclamation mark, `loading` a spinner, and `default` none. It is `aria-hidden`, so the title has to say what happened. In your own `Toast` composition, render `<ToastIcon type={item.type} />` before the title.
- The region takes no pointer events: only the toasts themselves cover the page, so buttons beside or behind the stack stay clickable.
- Timers pause while focus is in a toast, and while the pointer rests on one for `hoverDelay` ms (300 by default). A pointer that only passes over doesn't hold them.

## Testing toasts and alerts

UI SDK announces toasts through two visually hidden live regions it appends to `<body>`: `role="status"` (polite) and `role="alert"` (assertive), both marked `data-ui-sdk-announcer`. They stay for the page's life and keep the last text they announced, so after a toast closes `getByRole("alert")` and `getByText("Saved")` can still find its copy there.

- Find a toast by its part, not by text on the whole page: `[data-slot="toast"]`, or `within(screen.getByRole("region", { name: "Notifications" }))` while a toast is showing (the region is only a landmark then).
- `npx shadcn add @eskais/test-utils` adds the helpers to `lib/test-utils.ts`. It needs `@testing-library/dom` (a dev dependency).
  - `getToast(text)` / `queryToast(text)`: the showing toast with an element whose text matches; both throw when several match, `getToast` also when none does. `queryToasts()` lists them, newest first, without toasts animating out.
  - `queryAlerts()` / `queryStatuses()`: `role="alert"` / `role="status"` elements without the live regions.
  - `isAnnouncer(node)`: whether a node is in a live region. `ignoreAnnouncer` is an `ignore` for text queries: `screen.getByText("Saved", { ignore: ignoreAnnouncer })`.
  - `readAnnouncements()`: `{ polite, assertive }`, what the live regions hold. A toast is announced about 200ms after it shows.
  - `resetAnnouncer()`: removes the live regions; UI SDK makes new ones on the next announcement. UI SDK exports no reset of its own, so call it in `afterEach`, after Testing Library's `cleanup`.

# Data display

Part of the `eskais-ui` skill.

## Description lists

- `DescriptionList` is a real `dl` of `DescriptionItem`s, each a `div` holding a `DescriptionTerm` (`dt`) and its `DescriptionDetails` (`dd`). Screen readers announce terms with their definitions.
- `layout="stacked"` (default) puts each term above its details. `"inline"` puts them side by side, the term at `--description-term-width` (33%), divided by rules, and stacks them again once the list's own width drops under 24rem: a container query, so it works in a side panel. `"grid"` lays items out in as many columns as fit at `--description-column-min` (12rem), never more than `columns` (3).
- An empty `DescriptionDetails` (nothing, `null` or `""`) shows an `aria-hidden` dash and reads `labels.empty` ("Not set"). `mono` sets ids and hashes in the monospace face.
- `copyable` adds a copy button after the value (`copyValue` when the details aren't plain text, `onCopy`): the value is a group named by its term with a `copy` action for agents, the button is hidden from them, and "Copied" (`labels.copied`) is announced. Pass `labels={{ empty, copy, copied }}` in the page's language.

## Stats and deltas

- `StatDelta value comparison` sits under a `StatValue`: an arrow (mirrored in right to left) and the size of the change in a soft tone chip, then your `comparison` ("vs. last week").
- `value` is a ratio by default, so 0.12 reads "12%"; `format` takes `Intl.NumberFormat` options or a function, `locale` the locale. Use the same locale as the `StatValue` beside it.
- Its sign gives the direction (zero is flat), or pass `direction`. The direction gives the tone: up is success, down destructive, flat neutral; `invert` swaps them for a metric where down is good, like cost or errors; `tone` overrides.
- Screen readers hear `labels.up/down/flat(formatted)` ("up 12%") and then the comparison, never the arrow or the colour. Override the labels in the page's language.

## Meters and progress

- `Meter variant="ring"` with a `MeterRing size` child (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) draws the reading as a ring with the value in the centre (`children` replaces it) and the label below. The root keeps `role="meter"` and its value for screen readers; the ring is `aria-hidden`, `tone` colours the arc, it fills the other way round in right to left and doesn't animate under reduced motion.
- `format` on the root (`Intl.NumberFormat` options, or a function of the value) changes the visible value and what screen readers hear together; `locale` pins the locale. `formatValue={(value, { min, max, percent, text }) => …}` on `MeterValue` or `ProgressValue` replaces only the visible value, with any node; `getValueLabel` on the root changes what screen readers hear. A progress bar's `value` and `percent` are null while it is indeterminate.
- The default text follows the locale as CLDR writes it: es-ES, fr-FR and de-DE put a no-break space (U+00A0) before the percent sign ("21 %"), en-US none. That is correct; change it with `format` only when a design asks for it.

## Tables

- `TableCell` keeps its text on one line up to `max-w-80`, with an ellipsis; when the pointer arrives at a cell that is cut off, its `title` becomes the whole text (a `title` you pass stays). Screen readers and agents always get the whole text.
- `TableCell wrap` wraps long text onto more lines instead, for descriptions and summaries. In a `DataTable`, a column takes `wrap`, `cellClassName` (classes on every body cell, such as a width) and `headerClassName`.

## Charts

- `ChartDataTable data labelKey keys` is generic over the row type, so rows typed by an `interface` pass as they are, and `labelKey` and `keys` must name their fields.
